newsitem.title: ITALY: Austria's Liebscher sees 6-8 nations in EMU in '99.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Liebscher sees 6-8 nations in EMU in '99.

text.p: Austria's central bank president Klaus Liebscher was quoted as saying on Friday he expected only six or a maximum of eight countries to be among the first wave of nations joining Europe's single currency on January 1, 1999.

"Only six, or perhaps eight, European Union members will be able to achieve monetary union within the set timescale. I don't think there'll be more," Liebscher said in an interview with weekly financial magazine Il Mondo to be published on Saturday.
Il Mondo made extracts of the interview available.
He did not specify which countries would be in the first group apart from saying "there will be two big countries and some smaller ones.".

"EMU can be achieved in two or more stages without a drama for anyone," he said, adding that it was currently being studied how to work out the relationships between "the hard core of the euro and the other member states."
He said that an EMS 2, "which will be decided politically at the next Amsterdam summit set for June, is practically already finalised."
